findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: A probe thermometer placed in an empty pan in the cooler read 54F. The cooler's digital read-out indicates 54F. All time/temperature controlled for safety (TCS) foods in the veggie prep cooler were recently placed in the cooler and therefore would not be indicative of the cooler's function. Time as a control will be used for TCS foods in the meantime until the veggie prep cooler is functioning properly. Foods must be used or discarded within 4 hours of prep/removal from walk-in or reach-in cooler. Inspector will follow up in 10 days to see that the veggie prep cooler is functioning properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC at the time of this inspection does not have a current CFPM certificate. They stated that they are in the process of being sent to a course but it is not for another couple weeks. Education was conducted. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts at the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

1) The meats in the reach in cooler in the front of the facility are observed with internal temperatures around 48F. 2) Lettuce, tomatoes and spinach are observed with internal temperatures of 50F in the left prep cooler in the front of the facility. Both locations were discussed with the PIC. Steak was discarded immediately as it was in its cooler since the day before. Sliced tomatoes were allowed to be put back in the walk in cooler as they were only prepared approximately an hour prior to observation. All other items were prepared and placed in their coolers between 2-3 hours prior to observation. These items will be allowed to remain in use until four hours has elapsed and then any remains must be discarded. This will correct the immediate violation. The issue of the coolers not functioning correctly will be handled under line item #33 of this report.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

1) The reach in cooler in the front of the facility was observed holding TCS foods at approximately 48F internal temperatures. 2) The left prep cooler used for vegetable storage and sandwich prep was observed holding TCS foods with internal temperatures of 50F. The PIC was shown both locations. The TCS foods in both locations are being discarded at the end of four hours from prep and time control is going to be used until repairs can be completed. Per the owner (via the PIC) Bormida was contacted during the inspection and should be at the facility the next morning to conduct maintenance on the coolers and bring them into compliance. A follow up is being set for the next available day after ten days to ensure compliance.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

The cubby used for storing knives in the sandwich prep area was observed soiled during the inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean the location and maintain it clean to prevent possible contamination of the cleaned knives stored here. The cubby was removed and cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact items are stored in clean locations.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

There is not an available sanitizer in the front of the facility at the time of this inspection. The PIC indicated that a wet rag is used to wipe the surfaces throughout the day. This is not a safe practice. The food contact surfaces should be wiped with a sanitizer regularly to prevent possible pathogenic growth on the food contact surfaces. Education was conducted and the PIC prepared a spray bottle of sanitizer for these surfaces to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The floors under shelving in the back room as well as in the walk in cooler are observed soiled and needing to be cleaned, specifically under shelving and near the walls.  The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that all floor are cleaned at a frequency that precludes the accumulation of filth.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee is observed to don gloves without hand washing taking place. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to review hand washing with all employees to ensure it is taking place when needed.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria.

On arrival the dispenser for sanitizer used at the three part sink is observed to not produce a solution with proper concentrations. The maintenance person was in the facility for a separate item and was able to work on the machine during this inspection. They were able to repair the machine so that sanitizer of effective concentration was produced prior to the end of the inspection.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Only one employee at the facility has a food handlers certification available for observation. The maintenance person indicated that they should be on a computer somewhere but none were able to be shown during this inspection for verification. Ensure that all employees that do not have a Certified Food Protection Manager card have completed food handler training and that they are available for verification on inspections.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

No CFPM is available at the time of this inspection. Hand outs were given during this inspection and the PIC is aware that a CFPM must be  present at the facility at all times of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands briefly (approximately 5 seconds) and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet. The observed procedures also only rubbed the palm and palm side of the fingers. Proper hand washing was discussed with the PIC (and employee) and they are instructed to ensure that safe hand washing takes place at all times. Wash all of the hands to include between fingers, under fingernails and the top of the hands to ensure that all possible contaminants are removed. Then use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet in order to prevent recontaminating the hands prior to food handling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival the sanitizer dispenser at the three part sink would not produce effective amounts of Quat in solution. Because of this the three part sink and available sani buckets do not register correctly on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. The jug of sanitizer was replaced and ran for several minutes. After this the concentration was observed at correct levels.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Test strips are only available for the buckets and sink of the facility which use a Quaternary Ammonia based solution. The spray bottle used for cleaning/sanitizing the meat slicer is a CL based sanitizer. Ensure that correct test strips are available for all sanitizers used on food contact surfaces in the facility. Follow up is being scheduled for two weeks for compliance.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

Food handler cards were not available for employees at the time of this inspection. Food handler cards were discussed and the PIC is instructed to ensure that all employees who do not have a CFPM certificate have at least a food handler certification.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket in the facility does not produce a color change on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. Bucket was remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.12: (A) Cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT may not be stored in locker, toilet, garbage, or mechanical rooms. Also they cannot be stored under sewer lines, under leaking water lines, under open stairwells, or under other sources of contamination. 

Multiple packages of single service lids are stored under the hand sink drain line behind the register. Inspector discussed with the PIC and the lids were moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

The mop is observed stored laying in the mop sink. PIC consulted and the mop moved so that the wet end is hanging and facilitates drying.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels present at the back handwashing sink. CORRECTED— Paper towels were provided upon request. Dispenser was refilled. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.comment: Signed employee reporting agreements are not available.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Probe thermometer is not calibrated. When placed in ice water, thermometer read 40F. CORRECTED- Inspector helped staff calibrate thermometer.
4-203.11 (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2oF in the intended range of use. (Pf)

Thermometer is not provided in drive-thru cooler. Ensure thermometers are placed in all cold-holding equipment.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0 ppm at three compartment sink. Sanitizer jug attached to wall-mounted dispenser was empty. CORRECTED- PIC changed jug, and sanitizer was dispensed at the proper concentration. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed meatballs hot-held at 125F, probed. PIC stated that meatballs had been placed in the hot-holding unit 10 minutes prior. Discussed reheating to 165F and turning up the hot-holding unit to maintain temperature at 135F or higher.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 (A)(1) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57oC (135oF) or above. (P)
